info.name: SecurityHub API
info.description:
Complete collection for the SecurityHub API (/api/v1), organised by module.

How to use it:
1. Bring the stack up (docker compose up) — the demo profile seeds two tenants.
2. Adjust the baseUrl variable if the backend is not on localhost:8080.
3. Run "Login (ADMIN)" in folder 1: the test script stores accessToken and userId in the collection variables, and everything else inherits the Bearer from there. No manual token copying.
4. Run folders 2 to 5 in order: each creation stores the id the next one uses.
5. Folder 9 uploads a file: Postman stores the file path and not the content, so repoint the file field at docs/http/scan-nmap-exemplo.xml before running it.

No secrets in this collection. demoPassword is the public credential of the local demo (backend/src/main/resources/application-demo.yml), which exists only in a database created on your own machine; any exposed deployment must override SECURITYHUB_DEMO_PASSWORD. accessToken, devToken, viewerToken and otherToken start empty and are filled in at run time.

Annotated responses for each endpoint: docs/api-examples.md. Browsable contract: http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description: register and login are public; /auth/me requires the token. Login stores the accessToken in the collection variable, so everything else works without manual copying.

item.name: Register — creates a company + first ADMIN

request.description: Public. The first user of a company is always ADMIN. The password is 10 to 100 characters. The e-mail is globally unique: repeating one answers 409.
Public. The test script writes accessToken and userId into the collection variables. Run this request first.

exec: // Guarda o access token na variável de coleção: nenhuma cópia manual é necessária.

request.description: Authenticated, any role.
Demo profile. Stores devToken, used in the 403 cases.
Demo profile. Stores viewerToken. VIEWER is strictly read-only.
Second tenant of the demo seed. Stores otherToken, used in the 404 isolation cases.

item.name: 2. Projects
item.description: Readable by any role; creating, editing and deleting are ADMIN-only. Sortable: name, status, createdAt, updatedAt (default createdAt,desc).

query.description: Outside the allowlist (name, status, createdAt, updatedAt) the value is silently discarded
case-insensitive contains on name or description

request.description: Paginated envelope. Check the sort key of the response to see which ordering was applied.
status is optional: absent means ACTIVE. There is no companyId in the body — the tenant comes from the token. Stores projectId.
Full replacement: an absent description clears the description; an absent status preserves the current status.

item.name: 3. Assets
item.description: Readable by any role; creating, editing and deleting are ADMIN-only. Sortable: name, type, environment, criticality, createdAt, updatedAt.

query.description: contains on name, description or identifier
API | SERVER | WEBSITE | DATABASE | WORKSTATION | OTHER

request.description: identifier is optional and unique per project (case-insensitively); blank becomes absent and never conflicts. A projectId from another company answers 404. Stores assetId.

body.raw:
{
  "projectId": {{projectId}},
  "name": "API de pagamentos",
  "description": "Processa cobranças, estornos e conciliação",
  "type": "API",
  "identifier": "api.pagamentos.acme.test",
  "environment": "PRODUCTION",
  "criticality": "HIGH"
}

request.description: Sending a different projectId moves the asset, as long as the destination belongs to the same company.

item.name: 4. Vulnerabilities
item.description: Readable by any role; creating and editing belong to ADMIN and ANALYST; deleting is ADMIN-only. Status changes exclusively through PATCH /status.

query.description: contains on title, description or cve
reaches the project through the asset
dueDate in the past AND status OPEN or IN_PROGRESS

body.raw:
{
  "assetId": {{assetId}},
  "title": "SQL injection no endpoint de busca",
  "description": "Parâmetro concatenado diretamente na query",
  "severity": "CRITICAL",
  "cvssScore": 9.1,
  "cve": "CVE-2024-12345",
  "discoveredAt": "2026-09-17T12:02:00Z",
  "dueDate": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z"
}

request.description: There is no status in the body: every vulnerability is born OPEN. cvssScore goes from 0.0 to 10.0 with one decimal place; cve accepts CVE-YYYY-NNNN or an empty string; an absent discoveredAt means now. Stores vulnerabilityId.
The assignee has to be an ACTIVE user of the same company; every other case is a 404.
There is no state machine: every transition is accepted. Changing to the current status is a no-op that writes no audit row.

body.raw:
{
  "assetId": {{assetId}},
  "title": "SQL injection no endpoint de busca de pedidos",
  "description": "Parâmetro concatenado diretamente na query; reproduzido em homologação",
  "severity": "CRITICAL",
  "cvssScore": 9.4,
  "cve": "CVE-2024-12345",
  "discoveredAt": "2026-09-17T12:02:00Z",
  "dueDate": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z",
  "assignedToId": {{userId}}
}

request.description: PUT never touches status or resolvedAt. An absent assignedToId unassigns.
Entering RESOLVED fills in resolvedAt; leaving RESOLVED clears the stamp. The same equivalence is a CHECK constraint in migration V5.
userId is deliberately not @NotNull: sending null is how an item is unassigned. After that the assignedTo key disappears from the response.
The same predicate as the dashboard overdueVulnerabilities card. overdue=false includes items with no dueDate.
The recent items panel is this listing, not a fifth dashboard endpoint.

item.name: 5. Comments
item.description: Nested under the vulnerability. Readable by any role; writing belongs to ADMIN, ANALYST and DEVELOPER; editing belongs to the author or an ADMIN. There is no comment deletion in the MVP.

request.description: The body carries only the text: the vulnerability comes from the path, the author and the company from the token. content goes up to 2000 characters. Stores commentId.
Ascending order by createdAt (ties broken by id), unlike the rest of the API: a discussion is read from oldest to newest. editable mirrors the server rule for whoever is reading.
Anyone who is neither the author nor an ADMIN gets a 403 with a specific message. The audit trail stores contentLength, never the text.

item.name: 6. Users
item.description: ADMIN and ANALYST. ANALYST is included because assigning a vulnerability requires choosing a user. Plain array, no pagination, always ordered by name asc.

item.name: 7. Audit trail
item.description: ADMIN only. Read-only: no endpoint changes or deletes an entry. Sortable: createdAt, action, entityType.

query.description: Company | User | Project | Asset | Vulnerability | Comment

item.name: Filtered by action, actor and window

query.description: LOGIN, LOGIN_FAILED, REGISTER, CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, STATUS_CHANGE, ASSIGN, COMMENT, ...

request.description: Fields whose name suggests a credential (password, hash, token, secret, ...) arrive masked as "***".

item.name: 8. Dashboard
item.description: Four endpoints, all merely authenticated: the permission matrix gives "view dashboard" to all four roles. Everything scoped by the company in the token.

request.description: openVulnerabilities is OPEN + IN_PROGRESS, not a status count. topProjects returns at most ten rows, ordered by total desc and projectName asc.
Plain array of 4 elements, with the empty severities present. It does not use the paginated envelope: it is a fixed-size aggregate, not a listing.
Twin of the previous one, with the four VulnerabilityStatus values.
Window [today - (days - 1), today] in UTC, both inclusive. opened comes from discoveredAt and resolved from resolvedAt; no series uses createdAt.

item.name: Trend with days above the limit

request.description: Answers 200 with "days": 90. The clamp is silent because a chart control cannot open an error box; the response echoes the effective window.

item.name: 9. Scan import
item.description: Upload, review, then confirm or discard. The upload creates nothing — only the confirmation creates vulnerabilities, and only for the findings that still have an asset at that moment. Run folders 1 to 3 first: the import uses the project and the asset created there. The file uploaded is docs/http/scan-nmap-exemplo.xml, which points at the identifier of the asset from folder 3 and at an address that is not in the inventory.

formdata.description: Form field; the backend reads it as a request parameter, so the query string works too.
NMAP_XML | ZAP_JSON | NUCLEI_JSONL. Declared by the uploader, never inferred from the bytes.
Point it at docs/http/scan-nmap-exemplo.xml on your machine: Postman stores the file path, not the content.

request.description: multipart/form-data with file, projectId and format. Nothing is created: the upload reads the report, looks for an asset of the chosen project for each finding (matching on identifier, case-insensitively and ignoring surrounding whitespace), marks as duplicate whatever the company has already recorded, and stores everything as a proposal. Stores scanImportId and the ids of the first and second findings.

exec: pm.test("porta aberta não vira achado", function () { pm.expect(body.totalFindings).to.eql(2); });

request.description: The import with all its findings, in its current state. Reading is open to any role in the company. The findings are not paginated: their number is already capped by securityhub.scan.max-findings.

item.name: Link a finding to an asset (ADMIN/ANALYST)

request.description: Only an UNMATCHED finding can be linked. The asset has to belong to the company, not necessarily to the import's project: a scan may have hit an asset registered in another project of the same tenant. The import counters are recomputed in the same transaction.

exec: pm.test("o achado passou a ter ativo", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql("MATCHED"); });

item.name: 409 — link a finding that already has an asset

request.description: A finding that is already resolved has nothing to change, and a DUPLICATE would not be imported anyway: offering the change would be offering a change with no effect.

Creates one vulnerability per MATCHED finding, in a single batch, and closes the import. Everything that was not MATCHED becomes SKIPPED. Duplication is checked again here, because another import may have been confirmed in the meantime. The trail receives ONE SCAN_IMPORT entry with the counters — not a CREATE per finding. Stores the ids of the vulnerabilities created.
This is not an idempotent success: the first confirmation created rows, and answering 200 here would tell a client that repeated the call that it created rows too.
Only a PENDING import can be discarded. Discarding a confirmed one would delete the report that backs vulnerabilities that exist.

item.name: Upload the same report again — all duplicates

formdata.description: Form field; the backend reads it as a request parameter, so the query string works too.
NMAP_XML | ZAP_JSON | NUCLEI_JSONL. Declared by the uploader, never inferred from the bytes.
Point it at docs/http/scan-nmap-exemplo.xml on your machine: Postman stores the file path, not the content.

request.description: The same file again: no new findings. The fingerprint is sha256(scanner:ruleId:target:cve) — severity and CVSS are left out because they change between scanner versions without the finding being a different one. A duplicate is skipped and counted, never merged: the vulnerability from the first import may already have a status, an assignee and a discussion.

exec: pm.test("duplicado vence sobre com ativo", function () { pm.expect(body.matchedCount).to.eql(0); });

request.description: 204 with no body. Despite the verb, nothing leaves the history: the import moves to DISCARDED and the findings stay there. What goes is the file on disk, removed after the commit.

PageResponse with the counters of each import and without the findings: a page of twenty imports carrying all the findings of each one would be thousands of rows to draw six numbers. Sortable: createdAt, updatedAt, status, format, sizeBytes, totalFindings.

exec: pm.test("a listagem não carrega os achados", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().content[0]).to.not.have.property("findings"); });

formdata.description: Form field; the backend reads it as a request parameter, so the query string works too.
NMAP_XML | ZAP_JSON | NUCLEI_JSONL. Declared by the uploader, never inferred from the bytes.
Point it at docs/http/scan-nmap-exemplo.xml on your machine: Postman stores the file path, not the content.

request.description: Uploading, linking, confirming and discarding are ADMIN or ANALYST: whoever can create a vulnerability through a form can create a batch from a file. The multipart goes complete on purpose — projectId and format are resolved before the role check, and an incomplete body would return 400 without the rule ever running.
404 and never 403, like the rest of the API: a 403 would confirm that the id exists. This holds for the five endpoints that take an id.

item.name: 10. Negative cases
item.description: They all answer with the ApiError envelope. Run folders 1 to 5 first: these cases depend on the captured variables.

request.description: Body from RestAuthenticationEntryPoint: code UNAUTHORIZED, message "Autenticação necessária".
A token with another signature, an expired one or one from an inactive user: the same body as the previous case. The response does not say which case occurred.
message "Credenciais inválidas". A non-existent e-mail, a wrong password and a deactivated user give the same response, and the response time is comparable in all three cases.
Projects are ADMIN-only. Generic body: code FORBIDDEN, message "Acesso negado". The check lives in the service, not only in the controller.

item.name: 403 — DEVELOPER changing the status of someone else's item

request.description: The DEVELOPER ownership rule. Specific message: "Você só pode alterar o status de vulnerabilidades atribuídas a você". It can only happen inside your own company — an id from another tenant would already have come out as a 404. Run the request that assigns the item to the ADMIN first. An unassigned item gives the same 403.

exec: pm.test("mensagem é a da regra de propriedade", function () {

request.description: VIEWER is strictly read-only.
The trail is ADMIN-only.

404 and not 403 on purpose. A 403 would confirm that the row exists: by sweeping ids an attacker would map which ones are taken across the whole database without seeing a single piece of data, and the API would become an enumeration oracle. With a 404, a resource from another company is indistinguishable from one that does not exist.

item.name: 404 — delete a resource from another company

request.description: The same rule holds for GET, PUT, PATCH and DELETE.
References in the body follow the same rule: "Projeto 999999 não encontrado".
An unknown user, one from another company and a deactivated one are the same 404: the caller must not learn which of the three it is.
Case-insensitive comparison, within the company: "Já existe um projeto com esse nome nesta empresa".
Uniqueness per project: "Já existe um ativo com esse identificador neste projeto".
E-mail uniqueness is global, not per company (ADR 0004).

item.name: 409 — delete a project that has assets

request.description: "O projeto possui N ativo(s) e não pode ser excluído". Children are never deleted by a silent cascade.

item.name: 409 — delete an asset that has vulnerabilities

request.description: "O ativo possui N vulnerabilidade(s) e não pode ser excluído".
code VALIDATION_ERROR, message "Dados inválidos", fieldErrors with the field and the message.
Expects four fieldErrors: assetId required, title out of range, severity required and cvssScore outside 0.0–10.0. The order of the array is not guaranteed.
code BAD_REQUEST, message "Requisição malformada", with NO fieldErrors: the failure is in deserialisation and happens before validation runs.

item.name: 400 — incompatible type in the query string

request.description: The same case as the previous one: BAD_REQUEST with no fieldErrors.

item.name: 11. Silent behaviours
item.description: Two clamps that answer 200 instead of an error. Both echo the value actually used in the response, which is what keeps them visible instead of hidden.

item.name: a sort outside the allowlist falls back to the default

request.description: The property sent reaches Spring Data as an entity attribute path, so anything outside the module allowlist is discarded. Check the sort key of the response: it comes back "createdAt,desc", the default ordering.

item.name: a size above the maximum is capped at 100

request.description: PageableSupport.MAX_PAGE_SIZE. Check the size key of the response.

item.name: 12. Cleanup
item.description: In the order that respects the children rule: vulnerabilities (the one created by hand and the two the import created), asset, project. They all answer 204 with no body.

request.description: A deliberate exception to the children rule: the comments are deleted along with it, because there is no endpoint that deletes a comment on its own. How many were removed goes into the trail (commentCount in oldValue).

item.name: Delete the first vulnerability from the import (ADMIN)

request.description: Without these two the asset does not go: it has children again and the deletion answers 409 with the count. Whoever skipped folder 9 skips this request. Note: today it answers 409, because scan_findings.vulnerability_id references the row and VulnerabilityService.delete only handles comments and attachments; while that is the case, the following deletions (asset and project) fail too.

request.description: Without these two the asset does not go: it has children again and the deletion answers 409 with the count. Whoever skipped folder 9 skips this request.
